name: Aussie Racing Cars Super Series
intro: Don't let the size fool you, these things are essentially half-scale silhouettes of Mustangs, Camaros and Commodores, but they race like anything but a toy. Under that fibreglass body sits a 1.3-litre Yamaha motorcycle engine producing around 135 horsepower, mated to a sequential motorbike gearbox and revving out past 11,000 rpm, in a car that weighs only around 500 kilograms. That power-to-weight ratio is enough to send you well past 200 km/h on the straights of Australia's biggest circuits, all while running support to the Supercars Championship in front of a full house. It's tight, it's physical, and with a grid built around genuine parity, driver skill takes precedence over deep pockets or factory backing, so there's no hiding if you can't find the rhythm.

name: Brazil Karting Club
intro: Welcome to the purest form of wheel-to-wheel racing there is, no gears to worry about, no clutch to manage, just a Honda GX390 four-stroke sat behind you putting out a modest amount of horsepower through a single fixed ratio. With that little power on tap, every position you gain has to come from a cleaner line and a later brake, there's no engine to bail you out of a bad exit. It's an unforgiving teacher in the best way, learn to carry corner speed here and you'll understand exactly why so many professional drivers still call karting the foundation of everything they know.

name: British GT Championship
intro: Welcome to a venerable sportscar championship, the field is well represented here with second gen GT3s, GT4s and some gruelling endurance trials. To be among the best here you have to be familiar not only with the demands of your car, but others around you, all while minding other packs of cars fighting in front and behind you. Keep your eyes open!

name: British GT Open
intro: Welcome to one of the most eclectic grids you'll find on a British paddock, where full-fat GT3 machinery lines up alongside one of the fastest kit-car-turned-racer ever built. The Ginetta G55 GT3 brings a proper 3.7-litre V8, sequential paddle-shift and all the aero and slick-tyre grip you'd expect of a factory GT3 car, a serious, professional tool that rewards precise, disciplined driving. The Ultima GTR Race is a different animal entirely, a mid-engined missile that trades some outright downforce for astonishing power-to-weight, so don't be surprised if one comes flying past you on the straight only to hand the position straight back under braking. Managing that gap between the two philosophies, patience against a GT3 car, respect against an Ultima's raw pace, is what separates the drivers who thrive here from the ones who just survive it.

name: Campeonato Brasileiro de Endurance
intro: Welcome to Brazil's home-grown prototype battle, where P3 and P4 machinery share the track across some of the country's longest, most demanding races. The P3 cars sit at the sharper end, more downforce and more outright pace, while the P4s trade some of that performance for a more accessible, cost-conscious package, meaning traffic management becomes as important as raw speed. Multi-hour stints, pit strategy and reading where the class ahead or behind is in their own race will define your result just as much as any single lap. Respect the distance and respect the car in your mirrors, and this championship will reward patience over bravado every single time.

name: Caterham Academy
intro: Welcome to the peculiar world of Caterhams, your 270R weighs next to nothing and only puts out around 135 horsepower, but with no electronic aids and no bodywork to shield you from the wind, every corner becomes a lesson in pure sensation. The live rear axle and ultra-direct steering will force you to relearn the meaning of delicacy on the throttle, the slightest clumsiness gets punished instantly with a snap sideways. It's a demanding but honest school: master weight transfer here, and you'll have laid the groundwork for a career in single-seaters or GTs alike.

name: Caterham Roadsport
intro: Time for the Supersport 360R, quicker and wider on its footprint than the 270R, its 2.0-litre engine pushing the power-to-weight ratio to 360 horsepower per tonne, just as the name promises. The grippier tyres and reworked suspension will finally let you properly attack the kerbs, but don't get overconfident: the chassis remains as twitchy as ever, and any excess speed on turn-in will reward you with a beautiful spin in front of everyone. A stronger grid, a sharper edge, it's up to you to turn that aggression into rhythm.

name: Caterham Seven Championship
intro: Here's the top of the Seven pyramid, where you'll find the Superlight 360R, just as light and unbreakable as a 270R but honed like the 360R whose name it carries, with aero and setup work that no longer forgives any mistake in your line. This is the strongest field in the whole Caterham ladder, filled with drivers who've already proven themselves at the lower rungs and won't hesitate to have a go at you under braking. Keep the car settled, stay patient in traffic, and remember: in a Seven, it's always the driver who makes the difference, never the technology.

name: Copa Classic RS
intro: Welcome to the classic scene of Rio Grande do Sul, where a wonderfully mismatched grid of Chevettes, Unos, Gols, Passats, a 1965 Mini Cooper S and the sleek Puma GTE all share the same track. These are old-school machines with old-school manners: skinny tyres, soft suspension and engines that reward smoothness over brute force. Half the challenge is simply respecting the character of whichever era you're driving, the other half is out-thinking the very different car in your mirrors. Bring patience and a mechanical touch, and this grid will teach you plenty about racing outside your comfort zone.

name: Copa Fusca
intro: Nothing but Volkswagen Fuscas here, and nothing to hide behind either. The rear-engined layout means the back end will always have the final say, so smooth inputs and early throttle discipline are non-negotiable if you don't want to spend your afternoon facing the wrong way. It's a slow-car-fast kind of series, one where craft and car control count for far more than horsepower.

name: Copa Truck
intro: This is the wildest grid you'll ever share a paddock with: real highway trucks, stripped down, dropped low and turned up to over 1,000 horsepower, twice that of an average transport truck. Don't let the size fool you, some of these things will clear 240 km/h down the straights, so braking early and giving five tonnes of momentum the respect it deserves is essential. It's loud, it's physical, and wrestling a Stralis, TGX, Actros or Constellation through a proper circuit corner is unlike anything else in racing.

name: European Le Mans Series
intro: Just below the top rungs of endurance formats sits this contest, which throws in two different classes of prototypes to blast around a group of GT3 cars. The field can get snarled up very easily here, so avoiding collisions and off-track incidents is a must, tidy racing and watching out for safety cars can quickly turn the advantage your way!

name: European Truck Racing Championship
intro: The European stage for big-rig racing brings the same monstrous, over-powered Stralis, TGX, Actros and Constellation trucks to some of the continent's classic circuits. Braking distances are enormous and the trucks fight for space like anything else on the grid, so respect for the machinery and for your fellow drivers goes a long way. Keep it smooth, keep it patient, and enjoy the sheer spectacle of hauling that much weight around a race track.

name: F1600
intro: The Formula Trainers you'll encounter in this American Spec Series are a proper appetiser for Formula racing, they can be thrown around a fair bit on the track, and won't bite too hard if you overdo it; but you won't go anywhere quickly. There're no wings to keep you planted on the road, and the mechanical grip is low, keep it controlled, and you'll win.

name: Fiat Uno ASM
intro: A tight one-make battle awaits in the '95 Fiat Uno, no excuses about a slower car in someone else's hands here, it's pure driver versus driver. Light, front-driven and eager to change direction, the Uno rewards a clean, economical style far more than outright aggression. Learn to carry momentum through the twisty bits and you'll find yourself hard to pass, even in a field with nothing separating the machinery.

name: Formula 1 (Hybrid Gen 3)
intro: This is it, the best drivers in the fastest cars, ground-effects, ERS, DRS, nearly a thousand horsepower. If you can control the lightning-fast acceleration and cornering in these cars, you can drive anything. The racing here will demand all your speed, your positioning and your ability to battle, the ultimate prize awaits the driver who can master them.

name: Formula 2
intro: The road to F1 culminates in this all-or-nothing championship, featuring energy management, 4G cornering and DRS. These skinny-winged, lightweight rockets are incredibly sensitive and responsive, and the standard of driving required to tame these beasts is exceptionally high. Score high in this series and you might be ready for the very top.

name: Formula 3
intro: This championship is where open-wheeled hopefuls come to prove themselves against all the other hottest prospects, as it follows most of the F2 and F1 calendar. The Dallara-built cars will separate those who can handle the faster Formula machines from those who can't, and if you impress here, you might find more doors opening towards the top.

name: Formula 4 Northern Europe
intro: Time for an Atlantic-facing competition with the Formula Trainer Advanced, just as with the USFJ category, the Formula 4 series is all about finding mechanical grip in a twitchy open-wheeler. Take care not to overheat the slick rubber, if you lose the window, you'll find yourself falling back.

name: Formula 4 Southern Europe
intro: Prepare for a Mediterranean tour with the Formula Trainer Advanced, these circuits are well suited to getting the twitchy back end out, and snatching positions with well-timed switchbacks. Concentrate in the esses, pick your placement carefully during some of the longer straights, and don't be bullied off the track if you want to clear your rivals.

name: Formula 4 UK
intro: This Formula 4 series has a larger calendar than the continental series, so focus on scoring consistent points and keeping the Formula Trainer Advanced out of the wars. It's a delicate machine, and you can always claw back better points on the following races, so don't be too keen to bang wheels off the start line!

name: Formula Junior Historics North America
intro: Welcome to the North American home of a category that shaped the earliest years of open-wheel racing, the very same 1.0 to 1.1-litre front and rear-engined Formula Juniors that once launched future world champions on the other side of the Atlantic, now brought back to life on this continent's classic circuits. With so little power on tap, there's no engine to bail out a scrubbed corner, momentum is everything, and mechanical sympathy matters just as much as raw pace. These are irreplaceable pieces of racing history, so respect for the machinery comes first, but that's never stopped this grid from producing some of the tightest, most technical wheel-to-wheel battles in historic racing. Get your rhythm right in a car this light and this analog, and you'll come away with a driving education few modern categories can offer.

name: Formula Vee Germany
intro: Welcome to the German tour for Formula Vee, a series well suited to the capricious weather you can expect to encounter on the tracks here. Fortunately the Vee's come with road-going all-weather tyres, so rain or shine, you'll still be expected to balance the slippery rears and just shy of 100hp in racing machines that weigh less than a Smart Car!

name: Formula Vee North America
intro: A taste of single-seater racing awaits with a tour across some American greats, you may be surprised to find a humble 4-pot road engine and 5-speed box under the cover of these lightweight racers, but underestimate them and be prepared to face the gravel. The swing-axles on the rear will challenge your sense of road feel, and your patience with the throttle!

name: Formula Vee UK
intro: The twisty, rollercoaster rides of the UK series are an appropriate match for the Formula Vees; with locked differentials, twitchy handling and road rubber, you'll have your hands full making it to the finish line. Plan ahead, stick to your lines through the curves, and don't be tempted into any shoving matches, these nimble machines are delicate!

name: FRECA
intro: This regional European championship is tucked well into the middle of Formula 3 and 4, and the F4 spec cars you'll be racing against are capable of some very quick laptimes, you don't have a massive amount of power here, but neither do your opponents. Remember, smooth inputs, carry your speed through the slower sections and bag those points.

name: Ginetta GT4 Supercup
intro: Welcome to Ginetta's one-make proving ground, where every G55 on the grid runs the same Ford 3.7-litre V6, producing 355 horsepower, paired with a Hewland six-speed sequential paddle-shift gearbox and next to nothing dividing the machinery. At just 1,085 kg, the G55 is a genuinely serious tool, front-engined and rear-wheel-drive with real GT3-derived aero, so there's no car to hide behind here, only your own inputs. It's widely seen as a proper stepping stone into international GT racing, which means the grid is stacked with drivers who already know how to find the last tenth. Consistency, race-craft and a clean start will matter far more than outright bravery, because in a field this equal, the smallest mistake is the whole story of your weekend.

name: Ginetta Junior Championship Europe
intro: The European front for this spec series tests how well you keep a sub-1000kg four-pot in the points, only in this one you'll be pushing the G40 Cup across a variety of continental classics, then it's all about putting together what you've built up in preparation for a full circuit race at the end. Straight nose on the exits and watch out for any divebombs!

name: Ginetta Junior Championship North America
intro: This spec sports car series is all about picking your lines and feeling the flow-state of transferring weight from one corner to the next, the Ginettas may be small, but they're nimble and as well-equipped as any hardcore racing car ought to be. You may be thankful of the FR layout and Limited Slip Diff when plunging down tight corkscrews and bends.

name: Ginetta Junior Championship UK
intro: The home series for the Ginetta G40 Cup you'll be racing, this is where the car was designed, tested and it's 1.8L Zetec engine stressed to the breaking point. So expect similarly fierce and gritty racing on the UK's sportscar tracks. Much like the European series, conditions can change exceptionally quickly on these tracks, if you can handle it, so can the car.

name: Gold Classic
intro: A step up from the regional classic scene, Gold Classic gathers the same charming mix of homegrown metal — Fuscas, Puma GTBs, Gols and Passats — for a more prestigious calendar. The rear-engined Fusca and the fibreglass-bodied Puma GTB couldn't be more different to drive, one asks for patience with its pendulum-like weight, the other rewards a bit more bravery through the fast stuff. Whichever you're strapped into, consistency and car sympathy separate the podium from the also-rans in a field this varied.

name: Gran Turismo Hyper Series
intro: This is the summit, hypercars with the kind of power, aero and technology that blur the line between road car and prototype racer. Every circuit on this calendar is chosen because it can actually contain what these machines are capable of, and even then you'll find yourself right on the edge of what's humanly possible to control. There's no more room to learn on the job at this level, only refine what you already know, manage tyres and energy across a full stint, and trust a car that will reward total commitment as readily as it punishes the smallest lapse in concentration.

name: Gran Turismo Street Series
intro: Welcome to where it all begins, real street-legal machinery, straight off the showroom floor and onto some of the most iconic circuits in the world. These cars still carry their factory ABS, traction control and everyday road manners, so the racing is close and forgiving of small mistakes, but that also means there's nowhere to hide behind horsepower, it's your lines and your braking points that will decide the result. Think of it as the purest test of raw driving skill, learn to extract every last bit of performance from a car that was never built to be pushed this hard, and you'll be ready for anything the ladder throws at you next.

name: Gran Turismo Super Series
intro: Step up into proper supercar territory now, carbon-ceramic brakes, forced induction, and enough downforce and grip to make you question everything you thought you knew about braking distances. These cars ask for real commitment, the speeds are higher, the margins are tighter, and a moment of hesitation into a fast corner will cost you far more than it did in the Street Series. The grid here is stacked with drivers who've already proven themselves on the way up, so expect wheel-to-wheel racing at speeds that will keep your heart rate up for the entire session.

name: GT Revival Series
intro: This classic format will see you racing against many legendary GT1 machines on some of their equally famous tracks, these cars are still fierce, large-displacement machines , and will throw nearly 600hp at the road with barely any driver aids! Be prepared for combative racing, but remember the cost in the pits if you get too eager in wheel-to-wheel.

name: GT World Challenge America
intro: Big grids, big wings and big tracks are the name of the game in this American GT3 championship, the second generation cars all feature generous amounts of downforce, traction control, ABS and a variety of powertrains that duel with well over 500hp. You'll have to learn your car's advantages and weaknesses quickly, and maximise what you have to win.

name: GT World Challenge Europe
intro: The GT3 Championship comes to Europe for a huge variety pack of sprints, long races and even a full 24 feature. Much like the high-powered, high-downforce cars in this tournament, the mixed format offers a lot of points for drivers who can adapt to different race lengths and keep finishing well. Keep in scoring positions and you'll bag silverware.

name: GT World Challenge Sprint
intro: This Sprint series will have you fighting for the chequered flag in the latest generation of GT3 racing cars, the drivers here will push you to the limit as much as the cars will. Have confidence in the downforce and grip that these cars can give you, and success in these brackets could pave the way to the top tier of endurance racing, if you want it.

name: GT4 America
intro: Welcome to a strongly competitive GT4 contest, the cars in this class are not too far removed from road cars, but all feature well over 400 horsepower, track tyres and significantly lighter frames than their domestic siblings. The calibre of competition in this division is often a big step-up from club sports and one-makes. Be prepared for some tough battles.

name: GT4 European Series
intro: Flat sixes, V8s, V10s, FR, MR, you'll see it all with this GT4 competition, as it's very much like it's bigger brother series. No matter what you're driving in this field, you will have to maximise the package you're given, and be patient for opportunities even if the track doesn't favour your car, keep your nose clean and wait for right moment to pounce!

name: GT5 Intercontinental Clash
intro: Two continents, two very different schools of grassroots racing, brought together on one grid. The Ginetta G40 is a proper British club-racing staple, light, front-engined and built to reward a clean, patient style, while the Puma P052 carries all that Brazilian sports-prototype pedigree, a bit more edge to its balance and a bit more reward for the driver willing to carry speed into the corner. Bouncing between Britain's technical, high-grip layouts and Brazil's faster, more flowing circuits means you'll need to adapt your whole approach race to race, what works at home won't necessarily work away. Master both cars and both continents' worth of circuits, and you'll come out of this one of the most complete drivers on the ladder.

name: Império Endurance Brasil (2023)
intro: Welcome to Brazil's premier endurance stage, where P1 prototypes, GT3 and GT4 machinery all share the same track at the same time. Reading traffic becomes just as important as raw pace here, a backmarker GT4 car can cost you as much time as a bad lap if you misjudge a blue flag zone, so patience and awareness matter as much as speed. With multiple drivers, pit stops and fuel strategy all coming into play across the distance, this is as much a test of teamwork and consistency as it is of outright talent, one driver's mistake in the final stint can undo hours of clean work by the rest of the crew. Respect the faster prototypes, respect the class below you, and above all respect the distance, this is a war of attrition as much as it is a race.

name: IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge
intro: This US competition throws Touring Cars into the ring with a field of GT4 cars, for some hard multi-class racing between very different machinery. The GT4s are much faster than their TC counterparts, but no matter what car you're in, keeping pace without causing a crash is key, the season is long, and consistency is the winner.

name: IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge
intro: This multi-class sprint series is a good introduction to professional endurance racing, which is reflected in the variety of cars featured, with Prototypes, GT3s and GT4s all fighting their own battles at the same time. Traffic awareness and preparation is critical here, mind your overtakes and your mirrors, and stay out of trouble if you want to win!

name: IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship
intro: Welcome to the American Dream of Sportscar racing, where you'll do battle amongst LMPs, LMDhs and the latest GT3s to try and claim the crown. There are grand prixes, sprints and endurance races to test your mettle throughout the season. Top level racers congregate here and they will make you fight for every position.

name: Indy NXT
intro: This championship is the highest tier of 'Road to Indy' competitions, but you'd be foolish to write this off as a feeder series. These American open-wheelers are straight-line missiles coated in carbon fibre and are no less capable than their Formula 2 relatives. They will demand precision and caution, as will your competing drivers, be prepared!

name: Intercontinental GT Challenge
intro: This competition is the full-fat endurance roster for the GT3s, and these Gen 2 machines will be expected to be driven across 12 hour runs, 1000km hurdles and 24 hour marathons. Ensure you get plenty of practice in, dial in your setup, choose your pit strategies carefully, and concentrate on finishing the race. Plan ahead and the points will follow.

name: KZ Karting World Championship
intro: Step up into the fastest, most demanding class in the sport, the same 125cc two-stroke platform, but now backed by a hand-operated six-speed sequential gearbox producing around 52 horsepower. Suddenly there's a clutch to manage off the line, gearshifts to time perfectly on corner exit, and a machine that will punish a lazy heel-and-toe every bit as much as a bad entry. It's widely considered the closest thing to real single-seater racing on four small wheels, master it and you'll have nothing left to prove about your car control.

name: Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europe
intro: The Huracan EVO2s may be a little more comfortable in their home region than across the Atlantic, but they're still ferocious straight-line machines that'll demand strong braking and the ability to get the nose pointed early to properly fling them out of the chicanes. Mind your markers and don't get too greedy on the brakes in this one-make series!

name: Lamborghini Super Trofeo North America
intro: This one-make series is a bridge between GT4 and GT3 racing, with aggressive Lamborghini Huracan EVO2s that will happily put the hammer down on the straights, but will need a firm hand in the slower sections; they're not as agile or planted as the GT3s. Take full advantage of the ABS and TC and be aware of getting squeezed on the tighter bends.

name: Ligier European Series
intro: This exclusive series might deceive at first, but the Ligiers are not trackday tourist cars, hard slicks, an endurance fuel tank and over 350hp will quickly disabuse you of that notion! The cars reflect the competition; full sized circuits, keen drivers and a comprehensive examination of how you keep a fast, mid-engined car on the track and in the points.

name: Lurani Trophy Formula Junior
intro: Welcome to a genuine piece of motorsport history, brought back to life on modern European circuits. These Formula Junior cars, some front-engined, some rear, running tiny 1.0 to 1.1-litre engines, were the category that gave a generation of future world champions their first taste of open-wheel racing back in the late '50s and early '60s, and the Trophy that carries Count Lurani's name exists to keep that spirit exactly as it was. Modest power means momentum is everything, scrub off your corner speed and there's precious little engine to bail you out on the way back up, so smoothness and mechanical sympathy count for far more than outright bravery. Respect the machinery, these are irreplaceable pieces of history worth more than any trophy, and you'll find this grid one of the most rewarding, technical challenges in historic racing today.

name: Michelin Le Mans Cup
intro: This championship is a smaller endurance format than the likes of WEC or IMSA, but still has the classic tracks, prototypes, GT3s and pit strategies to whet your appetite. These machines have lots of downforce, setup potential, and if treated with respect, can be surprisingly forgiving and easy to drive. Just make sure you have enough in the tank!

name: Mini Challenge
intro: This popular support series for British Touring Cars will see you behind the wheel of a MINI Cooper JCW, if this is your first taste of hot hatches, expect understeer, scrappy handling and fierce power through the corners. Get it turned in early, keep up the momentum and make full use of what you've got, these cars expect to be driven hard.

name: National Formula Ford Championship
intro: The Formula Trainers in this spec series are much like their cousins in the American division: light, sensitive to bumps, and good teachers for your concentration and ability to find grip, when the car isn't helping with wings or limited slip diffs. The corners on these UK tracks will reward you if you can use the sensitivity to your advantage.

name: NTT IndyCar
intro: The USA's premier open-cockpit series features twin-turbo V6 cars, over 700hp, slippery, high-speed frames and push-to-pass systems. This is the ultimate showcase of American Formula racing, with ovals, street circuits and classic GP tracks. This competition is not for the faint-hearted, or the reckless, good luck and good racing.

name: Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie
intro: Eight rounds of racing, full grids of GT machinery, 24 hours at the longest circuit in motor-racing today. The Green Hell will break cars and their drivers across one of the most gruelling endurance formats, you need lots of concentration, clean driving, and plenty of luck to make it to the end. Finishing is a win, anything above is a bonus.

name: OK Karting World Championship
intro: This is where the world's best young talent gets measured, a single-speed, direct-drive 125cc two-stroke pushing somewhere around 34 to 36 horsepower through a chassis that weighs next to nothing. No gearbox means no distractions, just pure, unfiltered kart control, and with a grid full of drivers who've already been winning everywhere they've raced, the margins for error shrink to almost nothing. Get your entry speed and your exits right here, and you'll have proven you belong on the shortlist every junior single-seater team is watching.

name: Old Stock Race
intro: Welcome to a proper slice of Brazilian racing folklore, back on track today the way it was born decades ago. These 1979 Opalas carry the same big, torquey inline-six under the bonnet, wrapped in a heavy steel body that was never meant to corner like a modern tin-top, so weight transfer and momentum management will define your whole race. Contact is part of the culture here, these cars were built for door-to-door battles long before anyone worried about carbon splitters, so expect elbows out and paint traded in every braking zone. Respect the history under you, but don't be shy about using it, the Opala earned its legend by being raced hard, not preserved in a museum.

name: Ortona Karting Club
intro: Same honest, single-speed formula as its sister club across the ocean, the reliable Honda GX390 four-stroke doing the work while you focus entirely on where to put the kart. There's nowhere to hide in a field this close, drafting battles and last-lap moves are the norm rather than the exception, and the tiniest mistake in traffic can cost you half the grid in an instant. This is grassroots racing at its most genuine, come here to sharpen your racecraft against a paddock that takes it just as seriously as you do.

name: Porsche Carrera Cup North America
intro: Porsche's Cup series tests all participants very hard across the American circuits, the balance on some of these tracks can be on a knife edge, and you'll need to temper your straight-line braking to keep control of these 911 Cup Cars, they're not far behind their GT3 racing siblings in terms of pace!

name: Porsche Carrera Cup UK
intro: You'll be partaking in one of the most reputable one-make series across the UK's finest tracks, the Carrera Cup cars are all derived from either the 991 or 991.2 generation of Porsche 911 Cup cars, with their famously athletic rear-engined boxer sixes and rear wheel drives. The field will be close, and the benchmark is high here, keep your wits about you.

name: Porsche Carrera Supercup
intro: This is one of the official support series for the F1 calendar, and even if the 911 Cup cars aren't quite as fast as the main feature, they still attract prestigious talent and bring out some truly electric racing. Like any one-make series you are the main factor in edging out positions over your opponents, and the cleaner your drive, the bigger your rewards.

name: Puma GT5 Desafio
intro: A one-make showdown in the Puma P052, a proper lightweight sports racer built to bring out the best in Brazilian club racing. With even machinery across the board, this series lives and dies on braking points and racecraft, there's nowhere to hide if your lines aren't clean. Get your rhythm right in the Puma and the rest of the grid will be fighting to keep up with you, not the other way around.

name: Radical Cup Europe
intro: The Radical Cup features a fairly traditional format, with the MCRs on the grid resembling Group 6 cars, these 2.0 litre, tube-framed machines weigh less than a Formula Vee, but are much more potent off the line. Be aware of the liftoff oversteer in these cars, use the throttle to keep it under control, and bring it home in smooth fashion!

name: Radical Cup North America
intro: The North American arm of the Radical Cup is as intense and electric a racing competition as the European division, the MCR S2000 is the star weighing only 525kg, and will require you to be smooth and precise with 217hp under it. The American circuits will present as tough a challenge as your opponents will, so make sure you're in harmony with the car!

name: Super Trophy Trucks
intro: Forget everything you know about racing lines, this grid is about jumps, contact and full commitment. Every truck runs the same Chevy V8 pushing well over 650 horsepower, stuffed into a tube-frame chassis that weighs in around 1,300 kg, with enormous suspension travel built to soak up landings, not just corners. The purpose-built circuits blend regular tarmac sections with man-made ramps that send you flying tens of metres through the air, so throttle control on the way up matters just as much as where your wheels point on the way down. It's rear-wheel-drive, it's a little bit chaotic, and it rewards the driver willing to commit fully to a jump rather than back off and lose the spot, this is racing built for spectacle as much as for the stopwatch.

name: SuperKart World Championship
intro: Forget everything you thought you knew about karts, these 250cc machines run on full-scale, 1.5 km-plus circuits and hit speeds that put them in the same conversation as production-based race cars. The extra displacement and full aero package mean serious top speed down the straights, but the karts remain tiny and low, so braking points come up faster than your eyes will initially believe. This is the very top of the karting pyramid, physically and mentally, respect the speed and you'll discover one of the most underrated disciplines in all of motorsport.

name: TSI Cup Brasil
intro: Welcome to a genuinely accessible entry point into circuit racing, built around two of the most familiar cars on Brazilian roads. Both the Polo and the Virtus run the same 1.0-litre TSI three-cylinder turbo, good for around 128 horsepower on ethanol, so the fight comes down almost entirely to who brakes latest and carries the most momentum, not who's got the bigger engine. It's front-wheel-drive racing in its purest, most tactical form, drafting on the straights, blocking into the corners, and looking for every inch through traffic. Cut your teeth here and you'll leave with the racecraft habits that translate to just about anything with a steering wheel.

name: TSI Cup Europe
intro: The European chapter of the TSI ladder brings that same close, front-wheel-drive philosophy to the continent's classic club circuits. Same Polo, same Virtus, same modest turbocharged three-cylinder under the bonnet, which means the grid stays tight and the racing stays about the driver, not the chassis balance sheet. Expect slipstream battles into every braking zone and a field where a single mistake can drop you five positions in the blink of an eye. It's an unglamorous recipe on paper, and an absolutely brilliant one on track.

name: TSI Cup World
intro: The flagship of the family steps things up with the GTS-spec Polo and Virtus, their 1.4-litre turbocharged engine putting out around 150 horsepower, enough extra punch to sharpen up every overtake without losing the series' close, hard-fought character. Running across circuits on multiple continents, this is where the best from the regional TSI Cups come to measure themselves against each other, so expect the racecraft to be sharper and the mistakes to be punished harder. Learn to manage a longer, more physical season across very different tracks and climates, and you'll come out the other side a genuinely complete driver.

name: Turismo Carretera
intro: Welcome to one of the most storied championships in South American motorsport, where the road-going Cruze and Corolla you see on the grid are really just fibreglass silhouettes, faithful in shape but hiding a purpose-built tubular chassis and a spec inline-six engine underneath. That engine puts out somewhere around 500 horsepower, a huge number for a car this heavy, and it's built to a single regulated formula so the fight stays about the driver rather than the badge on the nose. These cars are big, torquey and old-school to drive, momentum and car placement will win you more positions than late braking ever will. It's a demanding, physical style of racing with a fiercely loyal following, earn respect here and you've earned it in one of the toughest paddocks anywhere.

name: USF Juniors
intro: The Formula Trainer Advanced series is bigger, faster and broader than the lower divisions, giving you more power and slick tyres, and expecting more from you in turn, with full length tracks and much more to lose if you mess it up. Preserving your momentum on exit and finding that balance with the nose and the grip is still paramount here.

name: USF Pro 2000
intro: Get ready for a power to weight ratio of 464 hp/tonne, gritty oval racing, serpentine GP tracks and the tight-knit racing that Formula 3 machines bring to the table. The Dallara F301s and F309s in this field are very evenly matched, with the latter only featuring slightly better aero and an extra gear in their box. But a good driver is the difference maker here.

name: USF2000
intro: Welcome to the natural evolution of Kart Racing, These F4 Grade cars aren't very powerful with sub 200hp, but they're an excellent midway between Karts and faster Formulas. It's all about balance with these cars, they're light, lively and fantastic for refining both your offensive and defensive racing.

name: World Endurance Championship
intro: This is the final test of your endurance skills, whether you're an LMDh specialist with 600hp hybrids, or a GT3 Gen2 star scrapping with over 500hp delivered the old-fashioned way. Whichever you're driving, the overall winner is the driver that doesn't break down, crash, or chew through too much rubber. Keep calm and prepare yourself.
